title: "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic (Bank 2)
plain: The computer is watching the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 2) and is seeing a signal that cuts in and out. This sensor tells the computer which valve lift mode the rocker arms are actually in.
symptoms: Variable valve lift may be disabled
Possible loss of power at higher rpm

causes.name: Loose connector or chafed wire that loses contact over bumps
Rocker arm actuator position sensor failing on and off

checks: Wiggle the wiring for the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 2) with the engine running while watching live data
Check connector pins for corrosion or spread terminals
Note when it happens (hot, cold, bumps) to narrow it down
fix: Repair the loose or corroded connection; replace the rocker arm actuator position sensor if the wiring is solid.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage "B" Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the actuator supply voltage "B" circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. This is a shared power feed the computer uses to run several actuators, such as solenoids and valves.
symptoms: Several systems may stop working at once
Reduced power or limp mode possible

causes.name: A shorted actuator pulling the supply voltage down
Blown fuse or failed relay in the supply circuit
Wiring short or open in the supply circuit

checks: Inspect the wiring in the actuator supply voltage "B" circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Find the shorted actuator or wire on the shared supply and repair it, then replace any blown fuse.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage "B" Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the actuator supply voltage "B" circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. This is a shared power feed the computer uses to run several actuators, such as solenoids and valves.
symptoms: Several systems may stop working at once
Reduced power or limp mode possible

causes.name: A shorted actuator pulling the supply voltage down
Blown fuse or failed relay in the supply circuit
Wiring short or open in the supply circuit

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the actuator supply voltage "B" circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Find the shorted actuator or wire on the shared supply and repair it, then replace any blown fuse.

title: Injection Pump Timing Offset
plain: On a diesel, the fuel injection pump timing is off from where the computer expects it to be.

causes.name: Injection pump timed incorrectly after service
Worn timing belt or chain, or slipped timing
Faulty pump timing or position sensor

checks: Check whether the pump or timing belt was recently serviced
Compare actual and desired timing in live data
fix: Re-time the injection pump; replace the timing parts or pump if worn.

title: Injection Pump Timing Calibration Not Learned
plain: The diesel injection pump timing has not been calibrated (learned) by the engine computer, often after a part was replaced.

causes.name: Calibration not done after replacing the pump or computer

checks: Ask whether the pump or engine computer was recently replaced
Run the timing relearn with a capable scan tool
fix: Perform the injection pump timing calibration with a scan tool.

title: Injection Pump Fuel Calibration Not Learned
plain: The diesel injection pump fuel delivery calibration has not been learned by the engine computer.
symptoms: Rough running, smoke or reduced power possible

causes.name: Calibration not done after replacing the pump or computer

checks: Ask whether the injection pump or computer was replaced
Enter the pump calibration data with a scan tool
fix: Program the injection pump calibration into the engine computer.

title: Air Cleaner Inlet Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the air cleaner inlet control circuit and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. Some engines use a flap at the air filter box to switch between cold and warm air or to quiet the intake.
symptoms: Usually little change in how the car drives

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the air intake flap actuator
Broken or chafed wire in the air cleaner inlet control circuit
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the air cleaner inlet control circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the air intake flap actuator.

title: Cylinder 5 Injector Data Incompatible
plain: The engine computer has correction values for the cylinder 5 fuel injector that do not match what it expects. This usually happens after an injector or the computer is replaced and not coded correctly.
symptoms: Rough idle or knocking from uneven fueling

causes.name: New injector installed without entering its code into the computer
Engine computer replaced or reprogrammed without injector data

checks: Read the code printed on each injector and compare it with what is stored in the computer
Ask whether injectors or the engine computer were recently replaced
fix: Program the correct injector codes into the engine computer with a capable scan tool.

title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector "A" Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the exhaust aftertreatment fuel injector and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. Some diesels spray a little fuel into the exhaust to heat and clean the particulate filter.
symptoms: Particulate filter cleaning may not happen
Reduced power if the filter clogs

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the exhaust fuel injector (doser)
Broken or chafed wire in the exhaust aftertreatment fuel injector circuit
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the exhaust aftertreatment fuel injector, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the exhaust fuel injector (doser).

title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector "A" Performance
plain: The exhaust aftertreatment fuel injector is not responding the way the computer expects. Some diesels spray a little fuel into the exhaust to heat and clean the particulate filter.
symptoms: Particulate filter cleaning may not happen
Reduced power if the filter clogs

causes.name: Clogged or carbon-fouled exhaust fuel injector
Low fuel supply pressure to the injector

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the exhaust aftertreatment fuel injector reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Clean or replace the exhaust fuel injector and check its fuel supply.
